additional_info.subject: ID0451267-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP/S8 170002461] Charger is offline CRM:02889000668
additional_info.body:
Hi Chlöe, good morning.
I sent this information to the regional colleagues. Please reach out to them for updates.
To check if the BT3 is good or not, please do the following:
Remove these 2 cables from the PLC cartridge and
Measure between the + and - for ~1kOhm.
If you don't measure the ambient temperature it should be replaced.
If you measure the ~1kOhm, then please try to reinsert the cables and if it works again.
If it still doesn't work, please try replacing the BT3.
If it still doesn't work, please take a look at the back side of the KF6 and understand if there are any bended pins (very unlikely) and unbend them.
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: RE: ID0451267-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP/S8 170002461] Charger is offline CRM:02889000668
additional_info.body:
Hi Monica, good afternoon.
What I see from the logs is the following:
|BT1-T=-34.2|
BT2-T=35.2|
BT3-T=51.8
|BT4-T=46.4|BT5-T=45.4
As you can see, the BT1 is not reading properly, we need to check that one. What I see is that the BT3 is very hot, depending on the position of the charger this can happen, I believe that this is correct since BT4 and BT5 are also values very high >45ºC.
Was there any maintenance performed on this charger? If the filters are clogged this is the answer, if they replaced the BT3 and it’s still persisting then it is a real temperature issue.
I would start from the filters.
With best regards,

additional_info.body:
Good afternoon colleagues,
I am reaching out as Sicharge D Expert from the Technical Support Team in regards of ticket
ID0451267
for charger
MP/S8 170002461.
The ticket was handed over to me on 11.11.2025, and I noticed the charger was still presenting the
temperature lower limit error
flag
and errors on DC1.
I connected to the charger remotely via SSH, and noticed that there was a communication issue with the SECC for DC1. I rebooted the charger on 11.11.2025 afternoon, and the communication was re-established. Since then, both outlets were available, and charging sessions were performed on both outlets since.
In regards of the
temperature lower limit error,
which is still active, I had a check in the logs:
2025-11-13T13:48:54.584501+00:00 [FW080005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [TLG] |Tstamp=1763041691|Mains-P=13.2|DC1-P=0|DC2-P=0|DC3-P=0|DC4-P=0|Ovheat=0|Mfan=0|Afan=0|EB1=1|
BT1-T=-30.8|BT2-T=33.4
|BT3-T=49.9|BT4-T=45.5|BT5-T=45.1|MFan-T=INVAL|
BT1-H=80|BT2-H=26|
The temperature detected by BT1 is -30.8 degrees, in comparison with all the other temperatures which are somehow aligned. This is the value which is setting the
temperature lower limit error.
The Humidity value detected by BT1 is 80%, compared to the Humidity value detected by BT2, which is 26%.
I believe that the output cables from BT1 of temperature and humidity might be swapped.
As per electric schemes, the humidity signal cable of BT1 is the green cable, which is connected first in the connector XD6.2D and from XD6.2C to the KF10-X10.I2, while the temperature signal cable is the yellow cable connected first to XD6.4D and from XD6.4C to KF10-X10.I1.
Could you please verify that such connections are not switched? As far as I understood, BT1 was replaced as well, it is correct? Please check the connections both on the LOGO KF10 and on the XD6 connector.
In case the connections are correct, it would be necessary to disconnect the two cables and measure the DC volt values (range 0-10V).
I attach here a visual reference of the connections to the XD6:
Please let me know if you need remote support on the day of the activity, and we can schedule a meeting.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you!
